# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Appeal of Denial — Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)**
**Member:** Riley Grant | **Member ID:** W485404613
**Reference Number:** POC-5767D9118E-71989
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-09
**Governing Policy:** EVH CG 2734.CC Outpatient Major Joint Arthroplasty (Hips and Knees), https://countycare.com/wp-content/uploads/ECG_2734.CC-for-Outpatient-Major-Joint-Arthroplasy-Hips-and-Knees-ver-Dec-25.pdf

Dear CountyCare Appeals Department,

I am writing to request reconsideration of the denial of my prior authorization for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446). My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the records already in the plan's possession meet the plan's own published criteria.

## Why I believe the denial should be reversed

The denial notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I have reviewed the plan's own guideline, EVH CG 2734.CC, and I believe my records meet the clinical findings the plan itself lists as supporting the need for this surgery.

The guideline states:

> "● Effusions ● Acute fracture ● Avascular necrosis ● Joint space narrowing or large osteophytes on imaging ● Severe sclerosis or deformity ● Bone on bone contact WITH At least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (6,16,17):"

My MRI of the knee, dated 2026-05-30, documented "full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition" and a Kellgren-Lawrence grade of 4 medially. This is a direct match to two of the imaging findings the plan's own guideline lists: bone-on-bone contact, and joint space narrowing.

On the non-surgical treatment requirement, my medical record documents:
- NSAID use for 8 months (2026-05 through 2026-07 and continuing), with inadequate relief — well beyond the 12-week threshold the guideline requires;
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-19, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief;
- Supervised physical therapy from 2026-05-15 to 2026-07-10 (8 weeks, 18 visits), focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, per the physical therapy discharge note.

Taken together, these records show non-surgical treatment well in excess of the 12 weeks referenced in the plan's own guideline, combined with imaging findings the guideline lists as supportive.

I also want to note that the guideline states:

> "● Where a specific clinical indication is not directly addressed in this guideline, medical necessity determination will be made based on widely accepted standard of care criteria."

and

> "These criteria are supported by evidence-based or peer-reviewed sources such as medical literature, societal guidelines, and state/national recommendations."

My symptoms — 9 months of progressive pain unrelieved by rest, inability to climb stairs without assistance, and waking 3-4 times nightly with pain — along with a physical exam showing positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion, reflect the kind of functional decline that standard orthopedic practice recognizes as supporting surgical treatment when conservative care has failed.

## Request for the specific criteria applied

I understand that CountyCare uses InterQual criteria to review requests like mine. InterQual is licensed software, not a public document, but I have a right to see the specific criteria used to deny my claim. Under federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules, the plan must provide me, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion relied on in my determination. I am formally requesting, in writing, the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination, so that I and my surgeon can respond to it directly.

## What I am asking for

I ask that CountyCare reverse the denial and approve the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) as requested by Dr. Marchetti, or, at minimum, provide a written explanation of exactly which criteria in EVH CG 2734.CC or the InterQual criteria my records fail to meet, along with the missing documentation, so that my surgeon and I can address it.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-05. I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if that address is unclear, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

Please contact me if you need any additional information from me or from Dr. Marchetti's office.

Sincerely,

________________________
Riley Grant
Member ID: W485404613
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [date of submission]

**Enclosures:** [Copy of denial notice; MRI report dated 2026-05-30; physical therapy discharge note; surgeon's letter of medical necessity, if available]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
